craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta of landing — rest, fulfillment, no-other-standing; autonomy dawning mid-proof. Quotative engine: Saying this / saying I — parallel placement (row 3); the this/I polarity is the doctrine, kept verbatim. Rejected: (a) merging the two sayings → killed: polarity collapse = doctrine collapse. (b) grows fit→becomes fit → killed: ucita-aptitude, L3 frozen. Read aloud: SAY-ing-THIS … SAY-ing-I … IT-grounds it-SELF.

lines: Saying 'this,' awareness grows fit to ground another's shine —
l4.sanskrit_cite: idam ity ucitaḥ saṃvit prakāśe 'nyasya vastunaḥ pratiṣṭhātmakatāṃ gacched aham ity ātmanā punaḥ

reads_against.argmap: How does consciousness take on grounding? → Consciousness fits itself to both poles: 'this' for the other's showing, 'I' for itself.
c1_essence: What never stood cannot stand another: consciousness fits itself to this and I, orders inert selves by double certainty, and completes severed grasping in self-rest (vv10-15).
The same self twofold — breath-bound atom, unbroken whole — gathers in one continuous end-ground where nothing shows more inert than shining (vv16-18).
